messages.subject: Large scale simulations of lynx
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently running simulations for an entire Eurasian lynx population in Central Europe that includes resident and dispersing individuals, the latter of which are about 25% of the total count.

As dispersing individuals have lower g0s and higher sigmas, I'm curious if it is more correct to model them as a separate population with different parameters, as is shown at the end of the secrdesign vignette for group simulations with males and females.

However, perhaps this separate approach is not necessary, as the dispersing individuals would have a lower weight in the results compared to the more abundant residents. For example, Ash et al. (2020) did not distinguish the groups when they simulated tigers.  

Thank you very much,
Stefano Palmero

messages.subject: Re: Large scale simulations of lynx
parts:
Stefano
I think you're right that it won't make much difference. On the plus side, it shows you're thinking, uses available information, and may improve the credibility of the results. So the judgment is up to you.
Murray
